gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much energy a 1 kWh power station actually delivers. Four named labs measured 850–910 Wh from 1,024–1,070 Wh units, which is 83–89% of the rating: Notebookcheck got 850 Wh from the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2, OutdoorGearLab 890 Wh from the same model, StorageReview 910 Wh from the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus, and nextpit 902 Wh from the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2. The same tests found 45–47 dB of fan noise under heavy load or fast charging, so 'nearly silent' holds only at light loads.
standout_why: ChatGPT's search returned no results and cited no pages, so there was no rival page to compare against. Its answer has no measured figures at all. It estimates 8–9 hours at 100 W for a 1,000 Wh unit without a source, and it calls power stations 'nearly silent' with no dB figure for either a power station or a generator. None of this comes from a named test.
decides: The measurements confirm ChatGPT's runtime rule of thumb. 850–910 Wh measured works out to about 8.5–9 hours at 100 W. They also give a concrete side-by-side for the choice. Bob Vila ran a Honda EU2200i inverter generator with a full-size refrigerator for 4 hours on about half a tank of gas, so it keeps going as long as there is fuel. A 1 kWh power station holds about 0.9 kWh in total. For outages longer than a day with a fridge, that points to a generator or a much larger battery. For electronics and camping, the power station's measured 83–89% delivery and 30–47 dB noise make it the better choice. On noise, the measured figures contradict ChatGPT's table: power stations are quiet at light loads but not silent under heavy load.

findings.label: Usable AC energy measured (Notebookcheck)
findings.source_title: Lighter, stronger and faster, but… Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2 power station review (Notebookcheck, Marcus Schwarten, 2025-12-21)
findings.note: EU 230 V version tested; the author notes the US version differs in some points. Continuous load of about 250 W until shutoff at 1%. AC charging took 1,110 Wh in (about 92%). Full AC charge just under 55 min without Boost mode.

findings.label: Fan noise measured (Notebookcheck)
findings.source_title: Lighter, stronger and faster, but… Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2 power station review (Notebookcheck)
findings.note: Measured at higher output and during fast AC charging. Much quieter at low loads. The article does not say whether the reading is A-weighted.

findings.label: Usable energy measured (OutdoorGearLab)
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 review (OutdoorGearLab, Kenji Mowrey, 2026-07-23)
findings.note: Discharged into a light-bar load bank; wattage not stated. Measured charging speed 1,097 Wh/hr. Fans described as 'frustratingly loud' near maximum wattage, with no dB figure.

findings.label: Usable energy measured (nextpit)
findings.value: 902 Wh of 1,070 Wh rated (about 84%); 1,020 Wh taken in to charge
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 im Test (nextpit, Thomas Kern, 2024-09-20)
findings.note: nextpit states 90% efficiency, but its own numbers give 902 / 1,020 ≈ 88%. Full grid charge in about 50 min in emergency mode.

findings.label: Noise measured (nextpit)
findings.value: about 47 dB in normal mode (charging and discharging); about 30 dB in quiet-charging mode
findings.note: nextpit says the reading depends on distance but does not state the distance it used. Quiet mode charges at about 260 W.

findings.label: Usable energy measured (OutdoorGearLab)
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 review (OutdoorGearLab, Kenji Mowrey, 2026-07-23)
findings.note: Test load wattage not stated. Measured charging speed 563 Wh/hr; a full recharge took 'almost 2 hours'.

findings.label: Usable energy and recharge energy measured (StorageReview)
findings.value: 910 Wh delivered from 100% to 0% (about 88.9%); 1,180 Wh to recharge from 0% to 100%
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus Review (StorageReview, Dylan Dougherty, 2025-01-02)
findings.note: Discharge load not stated. Measured UPS switchover just over 8 ms against EcoFlow's listed 10 ms.

findings.label: Noise measured (StorageReview)
findings.value: about 30 dB at 600 W load; about 40 dB maximum at higher loads

findings.label: Measured runtime on a refrigerator (Bob Vila)
findings.value: ran a full-size refrigerator for 4 hours on about half a tank of gas
findings.source_title: The Best Quiet Generators for a Peaceful Power Supply, Tested (Bob Vila; Mark Wolfe, Bob Beacham, Michelle Larson; published 2026-07-30, updated 2026-11-13)
findings.note: This is the testers' hands-on result. The page's 48–57 dB(A) figure for this model has no stated method, so it is not used here.

findings.label: Inverter vs open-frame generator noise (Mike Sokol, RVelectricity)
findings.value: 52 dBA inverter generator vs 68 dBA open-frame contractor generator (16 dB apart)
findings.source_title: Generator Noise: A Deep Dive into SPL! Part 2 (RVelectricity, Mike Sokol, 2023-06-13)
findings.note: Models, load and distance are not given for this pair. The article says the industry standard is A-weighted at 23 ft (7 m) and that outdoors the level drops about 6 dB each time the distance doubles. So the power-station readings above (1 m or unstated distance) cannot be compared directly with generator ratings taken at 23 ft.

findings.label: Runtime at 100 W implied by the measured capacities
findings.source_title: Notebookcheck C1000 Gen 2 review (low end); StorageReview DELTA 3 Plus review (high end)
findings.note: Arithmetic: 850 Wh / 100 W = 8.5 h; 910 Wh / 100 W = 9.1 h. These capacities were measured at heavier loads (about 250 W for Notebookcheck). At a light 100 W load the inverter's own draw takes a larger share, so real runtime may be slightly shorter. This supports ChatGPT's 8–9 hour estimate.
